harness.name: VulnHunter
harness.description: Capital One VulnHunter. Prompt-only Claude Code skills (/vulnhunt, /vulnhunter-fix, /vulnhunt-fix-verify) plus a Python agent that launches them headlessly and a benchmark harness.

components.doc: Batch vulnhunt runner: validates GitHub URLs from REPO_LIST.txt, shallow-clones each, optionally skips repos with existing results (--resume), scans in parallel (read-only unless --execute), and prints a summary.
Batch-scan utilities: REPO_LIST parsing, symlink-safe collection of each repo's own results dirs into a flat upload dir, and status reporting from each clone's JSONL scan log.
Miss analysis for the local benchmark: for each false negative, heuristically locate the losing phase from scan artifacts, then run an agentic Claude diagnosis that suggests a minimal prompt edit.
Per-finding detection history across benchmark runs (finding_history.json); identifies "stable" findings detected in each of the last N runs so --skip-stable can skip them.

Ground-truth file shape for the benchmark: a JSON array of findings. This shipped example is synthetic (three OWASP demo apps with placeholder commits); the judge compares each finding against a scan report.
LLM-as-judge for the local benchmark: one batched `claude -p` call per scan decides, for each ground-truth finding, whether the scanner's README.md report detected the same vulnerability.

Benchmark harness: load ground truth, dedupe (repo, commit) targets, clone at commit, scan in parallel, LLM-judge each ground-truth finding against the scan report, tally detection rate, update finding history.
Benchmark tally: detection rate (recall) overall and per vulnerability type from judge verdicts, plus cost/time/token aggregates; writes tally.json and BENCHMARK_REPORT.md.
Clones benchmark repos at a pinned commit (fast depth-1 fetch, then full-clone fallback), and shallow-clones HEAD for ad-hoc batch scans.
Shared constants for the local VulnHunter benchmark harness: paths, scan/judge worker counts, timeouts, model, 429 retry/backoff settings, and an atomic JSON writer.

Benchmark harness scanner: runs headless `claude -p "/vulnhunt <dir>"` per cloned repo in parallel, read-only by default, with 429 retry; symlink-safe handling of results dirs and logs in untrusted clones.

/vulnhunt orchestrator skill, the L0 of the scan logic: binds scan metadata, then dispatches one subagent per phase (recon, hunt fan-out, verify, reproduce+test+fix, sweep) and compiles the report. It does no analysis itself. Operating Principles and Investigation Discipline (VulnhuntInvestigationDiscipline) stay in effect in every phase.

The phase prompt file set of the /vulnhunt skill and how phases are loaded: install.sh copies vulnhunt/ to ~/.claude/skills/vulnhunt; the orchestrator resolves PHASES_DIR and each subagent Reads its own phase file.

Phase 1 recon subagent: maps the attack surface (files, sink inventory, input inventory, indirect dispatch, call graph + union-find partitions, authz gate audit, auth paths, threat model, trust boundaries, build swapping) and writes phase1_output.md, whose partition and inventory tables drive Phase 2 dispatch.

INJ (injection) class-group reference read by every INJ trace agent in Phase 2. Renders the dangerous-sink reference, the injection class hunts, the INJ-specific Gate 2b sanitizer verification, the INJ Gate 3 do-not-eliminate list and the INJ severity floor as MODEL control flow.

LOG (logic / crypto) class-group reference read by every LOG trace agent in Phase 2. Renders the sink reference, crypto / memory-safety / logic / resource-exhaustion / prototype-pollution hunts, the non-exhaustive "other patterns" sweep and the LOG Gate 3 do-not-eliminate rule as MODEL control flow.

NAV (navigation / authentication / authorization) class-group reference read by every NAV trace agent in Phase 2. The prompt sections are rendered as Prompt builders; the procedure they ask for (mandatory input gates, NAV gate exemptions, severity floor, missing-auth assessment, class hunts, post-trace audit) as MODEL control flow.

Phase 2 (orchestrator): forms hunt jobs = production partitions x class groups (INJ, NAV, LOG) plus one sink-driven audit agent, dispatches them in waves, then aggregates dispositions into VULN-NNN candidates. Prompt-only logic: the orchestrator model follows this procedure; nothing here is enforced by code.

Shared instructions every Phase 2 class-group trace agent (INJ, NAV, LOG) reads first: input-forward iteration rules, absent-input and auth-branch checks, HARD GATES 0/1/2a/2b/3 in order, severity tiers, output format. Prompt-only: all logic is carried out by the trace-agent model.

Phase 2b: adversarial (disprove) verification of every Phase 2 candidate, run by the model. Prompt-only logic: manifest, consensus-skip, nine checks per candidate, platform auth rollup, verdict table (CONFIRMED / FALSE POSITIVE), anti-merge rule, drop of false positives.
Phase 3a/3b: assign VULN-NNN ids, write one PoC per CONFIRMED finding (runnable or static trace), then one exploit test per finding; test outcome decides confirm / Code Smell / Potential / eliminate.
Phase 3c: for each finding with a passing exploit test, document a fix strategy for the report (no source edits). Includes the CWE-639 / platform-auth caller-scope fix guidance.

Phase 3d sweep subagent: for every confirmed root cause, grep the FULL codebase (source and sink patterns, transitive callers), triage every instance, and send each CANDIDATE through gates, PoC and exploit test; writes phase3d_output.md.
Phase 4: compile the final report (summary table, per-finding detail, code smells, sweep table, README entry point with exact header, links, cross-check) and apply the What-NOT-to-Report filter.

/vulnhunt-fix-verify orchestrator skill: reads a prior /vulnhunt scan, takes the developer's claim that some findings are fixed, and produces an independent per-finding verdict by static inspection of REPO. Phases 0, 1, 2, 4 (no phase 3). Prompt sections first, then the procedure the model runs.

Comment-file rules R0-R7 applied by phase 0 to every claim segmented from the developer COMMENTS file, plus segmentation and the claim-entry output shape. Rule IDs are cited in each claim's rationale.

Fix-verify phase 0 (pre-flight): argument shape, path existence via Glob, report layout, VULN ID lookup, best-effort HEAD metadata, COMMENTS evaluation under comment_rules R0-R7, then phase0_state.json.
Fix-verify phase 1: convert the prior /vulnhunt report into ${OUT}/extracted_findings.md, one "## VULN-NNN" section per ID in fixed_ids_in_report, plus relevant accepted comment claims.

Fix-verify phase 2: per-VULN static verification through four gates (sink_mitigated, reachability, class_eliminated, sweep_complete), verdict mapping, issue_comment templates, disposition_VULN-NNN.json.
Fix-verify phase 4: merge phase0_state.json and per-VULN dispositions, add INVALID_INPUT stubs for missing IDs, order by the FIXED argument, validate against verify_disposition.schema.json, write.
Agent namespace; no runtime procedure.
CLI entrypoint: --mode=scan clones a repo and runs /vulnhunt (ScanFlow in runner.pseudo); --mode=verify runs /vulnhunt-fix-verify against issue URLs (AgentVerify -> VerifyRunner).
Verify mode: recover an issue body's original text from GitHub's userContentEdits history. The oldest edit's diff field is a raw body snapshot; zero edits means the current body is the original.
Shared GitHub helpers for the publish and issues stages: REST API base resolution, owner/repo extraction from a repo URL, and the results-dir timestamp suffix parser.

GitHub REST + GraphQL surface for --mode=verify: read one issue, its edit history, comments and events, post a comment, reopen. Every fetch is bounded (CWE-400); one retry on 429/5xx with a fixed backoff.
Small one-shot JSON LLM calls (findings extraction, dedup, verify parsing) via the SDK with no tools: same-model transient retry, then one fallback model.

Shared SDK-event rendering for runner.py (scan) and verify_runner.py (verify): verbosity-tiered logging of assistant/user/system/task/result events (always credential-redacted) and per-session cost/turn totals.
Shared transient-error classifier (HTTP 429 / 5xx / overload) used by _llm.py and runner.py to decide whether an SDK failure is worth retrying. Typed status wins over message text.
URL helpers for clone and publish: inject a GitHub token only into matching-host (and optionally authorized-path) HTTPS URLs, and redact credentials from any text before logging/auditing (CWE-532).
JSONL audit-event and findings-event streams (local append-only files, optional stdout mirror). Every string is credential-redacted, None fields dropped, free text capped; ids are monotonic ULIDs.
Audit-stream converters: a cheap on-disk VULN count for scan_completed, and a pure converter from the issues-stage ExtractedReport to findings-event dicts (the Haiku extractor is never re-run here).
Anthropic auth providers behind one getValidToken() interface: API key (verbatim), Bedrock OAuth2 client-credentials (cached, refreshed after a fraction of its lifetime), Bedrock SigV4 (empty token).

Builds the Claude Code settings JSON (env + OS sandbox) passed to every SDK session (scan, verify, small LLM calls). Routes inference via api_key, bedrock_oauth or bedrock_sigv4; blanks proxies; optional OTLP telemetry.
Shallow-clones the target repo into the clone base dir (scan mode), or at a pinned commit (verify mode). The scan sees only the snapshot: no git history is fetched.

The shipped example config (copy to config.toml). Env VULNHUNT_<SECTION>_<KEY> overrides every value. Note: the example ships sandbox.enabled = false and issues.enabled = false, unlike the code defaults (true).

Loads AgentConfig from TOML + env (env VULNHUNT_<SECTION>_<KEY> > TOML > default), one frozen record per section. Knob reads here mark where each default is set; the knobs are rendered where they act (runner.pseudo, build_settings.pseudo).

Issues stage: extract -> ensure labels -> fetch open issues -> dedup -> post one issue per new finding. Per-issue failures are recorded, not fatal. Zero findings -> clean-scan receipt issue (posted then closed).
Issues stage, step 2: dedup new findings against open GitHub issues. Pass 1 (code): vulnfix-key marker match. Pass 2 (model): semantic compare, issues chunked to a token budget.

Issues stage, step 1: a small model turns the results README.md into strict JSON findings (Confirmed rows only); code fills PoC/test paths from the filesystem and computes vulnfix_key. Also holds the [issues] config section (IssuesConfig) whose knobs drive the whole issues stage.
Paginated fetch of open issues carrying a label (the issues-stage dedup pool). Pull requests are dropped; each page is retried once on 429/5xx; hitting max_open_issues fails the stage.
Fetch a published VulnHunter report from publish.destination_repo by sparse checkout of <owner>/<name>/: the newest *VULNHUNT_RESULTS* dir (--no-scan --issues) or an exactly named one (verify mode).
Render a Finding into a GitHub issue title + body (templates/issue_body.md) with sanitized attacker-influenced fields and machine-readable footer markers; also the clean-scan issue/comment.
Producer-side writer for <results_dir>/scan_manifest.json: findings, session cost and issues-stage outcomes, validated against scan_manifest.schema.json and committed atomically.
Publish stage: push the *_VULNHUNT_RESULTS_* dir into publish.destination_repo under <owner>/<name>/<timestamp>/<sha>/<results_dir>/, creating the destination as a private repo if missing.
Optional per-repo metadata tags for findings records. Precedence: CLI override > GitHub custom properties (via [repo_properties].github_property_map) > blank. Every GitHub failure degrades to blank.

L0 of the Python agent: run_vulnhunt launches the /vulnhunt skill (VulnhuntSkill.run) in one Claude Agent SDK session against a fresh clone, with cold-start retry and a continuation loop for background subagents. ScanFlow renders __main__._run_scan_flow (clone -> scan -> publish -> extract findings -> issues) around it.
Build identity (<short-sha>-<clean|dirty>) read from the generated _build_version module; "unknown" otherwise.
Body of the closed "clean scan" receipt issue (no findings). Filled by IssuesRender.renderCleanScanBody; placeholders written as <NAME>. Read by humans, not by a model.
Per-scan receipt comment appended to an already-open clean-scan issue. Filled by IssuesRender.renderCleanScanComment; read by humans, not by a model.
GitHub issue body for one finding, filled by IssuesRender.renderBody. Humans read it, and the footer HTML-comment markers are parsed later by /vulnhunter-fix and verify mode (issue intake).
Role-based GitHub token accessor (scan / reports). Standalone mode returns config tokens; broker mode reads <broker_token_dir>/<role>.json on every request (no in-agent cache).

--mode=verify orchestrator: fetch closed issues (+ edit history), reconstruct original bodies, extract markers, enforce one repo + one report per run, clone target, stage the named report, Haiku pre-flight for cross-repo references, one /vulnhunt-fix-verify session (VerifyRunner), then post verdicts / reopen and emit audit events.

Verify-mode inputs from a GitHub issue: the three machine markers (from the reconstructed original body), the post-close developer narrative, and the comments.md file handed to /vulnhunt-fix-verify (untrusted-wrapped).
Post verify outcomes to the source issues: verdict comment (with attribution banner), optional body-tampering archival comment, then reopen for NOT_FIXED / PARTIAL / INCONCLUSIVE. No labels.

Verify mode pre-flight: the scan model extracts unambiguous cross-repo references from developer comments as strict JSON; code coerces the result. Best effort: any failure returns [] (skill R2 catches the rest).

Verify-mode git/GitHub resolution: repo_hint -> clonable URL (allow-listed URL or exact alias, never inferred), additional-repo and target clones, and staging of the named scan report. Failures raise ResolveError.
Verify mode SDK driver: build the /vulnhunt-fix-verify kickoff prompt, run one read-only session with a fixed tool set, then classify verify_disposition.json (disposition / empty / schema-invalid).
Agent-to-scan-worker contract written at <results_dir>/scan_manifest.json. The agent validates before writing, the scan worker validates on read; every object is closed (additionalProperties false).
Per-vulnerability verdict file written by /vulnhunt-fix-verify at <out>/verify_disposition.json. Four gates per finding, a comments-file evaluation block, closed objects throughout.
Placeholder project-template entry point; prints a greeting. Not wired into the agent (agent/__main__.py is the CLI).

Top-level vulnhunter-fix skill: mode dispatch, mandatory first actions (Opus gate, version check, preflight, gh auth), the git/gh failure policy, task tracking, non-negotiable rules, phase-boundary checkpoints, and the Parse -> Plan -> Implement -> Verify -> Sweep -> Deliver workflow that calls each phase's prompt file.
Fork-mode access whitelist: users added to the private fork created for delivery (deliver.md step 3).
Static configuration of the vulnhunter-fix skill (github, git, verification, behavior, models, modes). Read by SKILL.md / prompts at run time; several keys are documented but inert (see notes).

Fork-mode repair agent: invoked between repair-loop attempts (verify.md Step 3) with the verifier's fix brief. Fresh-context, temperature-0 session that applies the brief, commits, re-runs tests and writes a result JSON.

Phase 5 (Deliver) prompt for the vulnhunter-fix orchestrating session: fork-mode delivery into a private fork (setup, dedup, triage, issues, PRs, tracking issue, cleanup) or in-place delivery (one PR per cluster on origin), both behind mandatory pre-delivery gates (honesty guards, completeness checklist, run-gates.py).

Phase 3 of vulnhunter-fix: TDD implementation of each finding (exploit demo -> RED test -> fix -> exploit blocked -> discrimination evidence -> regression -> scope check -> pre-existing test updates -> commit). In-place mode: one branch per cluster + interactive collaboration loop. Fork mode: one masked branch per finding + issue fallback.
Phase 1 (fork mode): parse VulnHunter results (local dir or repo URL) with scripts/parse_results.py, validate actionability, read PoC/exploit/README context, present a summary table, stop on errors.

Phase 1 of vulnhunter-fix in in-place mode: harvest vulnhunter-labeled GitHub issues (or a local RESULTS_PATH), let the developer pick issues/clusters, stage the full report from the publish repo, extract findings with a Sonnet subagent, hash vulnfix_keys in Python, and join issues to findings into .vulnhunter-fix/work.json.

Phase 2 remediation plan, mode-aware: in-place sequences a developer-picked cluster on one branch; fork delegates to plan_fork.md. Both modes then run seven mandatory rigor actions (graph, sidecars, tier, gates).
Phase 2 (fork mode): prioritize, live-code pre-check, strict grouping with masked branch names, conflict detection, per-finding assessment, plan table and user confirmation.

Test-quality reviewer: fresh no-context subagent invoked in Verify Step 2c; scores the security test against rubric rules R1-R5 and returns GOOD/WEAK/WRONG with an optional fix brief for the repair agent.

Phase 3c root-cause sweep: after Verify, before Deliver, walk every ROOT cause and hunt sibling defects via scripts/sweep-root-causes.py, then route siblings, downgrade tiers and fill verification-table column 8.

Bounded LLM fallback that picks a completeness tier when compute-completeness-tier.py returns LLM_REVIEW (Plan and Verify phases). Single-line JSON output parsed by parse-tier-judgment.py; retry once, then manual review.

Phase 4 (Verify & Repair) prompt for the vulnhunter-fix orchestrating session: stale-fix pre-check, three-step validation (security test / regression record / test-quality reviewer), repair loop, fork-mode escalation, then mandatory Steps 5-9 (tier re-classification, sweep, table, gates, validators).

CWE-class worker prompt for authorization findings (CWE-287/290/306/639/862/863/915); extends the common preamble with the canonical fix pattern, two-user discrimination, FULL-tier bar, anti-pattern downgrades and residual template.

Shared worker preamble: one root-cause group per worker in its own worktree, TDD cycle per finding (exploit -> patchability -> RED test -> fix -> exploit blocked -> discrimination -> regression -> promote -> scope -> commit).

CWE-class worker prompt for IaC/IAM configuration findings; extends the common preamble but replaces the Python TDD cycle with static-analysis-tool discrimination, no verify_ scaffold, and a tool-run regression check.

CWE-class worker prompt for crypto findings (CWE-295/326/327/328/330/345/347); extends the common preamble with the canonical fix pattern, a mechanical four-boolean trust-chain gate for FULL, anti-patterns and never-do rules.

CWE-class worker prompt for injection findings (CWE-22/78/79/89/94/352/434/502/601/611/918); extends the common preamble with per-sink structural fixes, reject-not-sanitize, exact-PoC discrimination, FULL bar and downgrades.

CWE-class worker prompt for resource findings (CWE-117/200/362/400/532); extends the common preamble with per-CWE fix patterns, pre/post discrimination, FULL-tier bar, anti-pattern downgrades and residual template.

Rule book (REQ-GAT-006): the 0.6 grouped-vs-split file-ratio fence that decides whether findings may share one PR. Consumed by scripts/anti-merge-check.py (Gate 5, run by scripts/run-gates.py with --strict before deliver.md's gh calls) and by the Phase 3 executor / plan.md grouping decision.
Allow / deny identifier lists and parameter floors read by scripts/crypto-trust-chain-checkers.py (REQ-CWE-009 algorithm_approved). A false result forces MITIGATION tier for the crypto finding.
Approved / denied key-source call patterns read by scripts/crypto-trust-chain-checkers.py (REQ-CWE-009 key_source_approved). Deny wins over approve; false forces MITIGATION tier.

Rule book (REQ-GAT-013): scaffold test name during RED->GREEN, promotion before commit, and Gate 7 scaffold-leak check. Consumed by scripts/check-committed-test-naming.py (Gate 7 via scripts/run-gates.py, pre-deliver); the promotion is carried out in prompts/implement.md (IP-Step H) and prompts/worker_agent_common.md (Step G).

Rule book (REQ-CWE-002, REQ-CWE-003): five CWE classes, each with CWE IDs, canonical fix shape, discrimination criteria, FULL-tier bar. Read by prompts/plan.md (Phase 2 CWE routing), prompts/implement.md (Phase 3) and the five prompts/worker_agent_*.md workers; also used by sweep-algorithm.md Pass 2 to pick the CWE class.
One parsed VulnHunter finding as emitted by scripts/parse_results.py; input to Plan, Implement, Verify, Sweep, Deliver. Open object (extra keys allowed); five required fields.

Rule book (REQ-HON-001..004): FULL / MITIGATION / WORKAROUND signal catalog, walked conservative-first. Consumed by scripts/compute-completeness-tier.py (deterministic classifier, Phase 4 verify); LLM_REVIEW routes to prompts/tier_judgment.md, which also reads this rubric as guidance.

Per-finding plan artifact from Phase 2 (Plan): strategy, files, projected tier + residuals, caller coverage, optional tier_judgment, crypto trust-chain booleans, chosen adapter language and CWE-class worker prompt.

Rule book (REQ-GAT-005): vulnfix-key derivation, marker shape, and Gate 4 checks. Consumed by scripts/check-idempotency.py (Gate 4, pre-deliver via run-gates.py) and vulnhunter_fix.delivery.compute_idempotency_key() (also mirrored by scripts/parse_results.py and scripts/issue_intake.py compute_vulnfix_key).

Rule book: cross-phase remediation-rigor invocations (scripts per phase), error semantics and back-fill rules. Companion to the "## Remediation-rigor additions" stubs in prompts/plan.md (Phase 2), prompts/implement.md (Phase 3), prompts/verify.md (Phase 4) and prompts/deliver.md (Phase 5); one method per phase section.

Rule book (REQ-CWE-004, REQ-CWE-005): per-language adapter (Go / Java / TS-JS / Python): detection, test command, deps, framework idioms. Phase 2 (prompts/plan.md executor) detects the primary language and injects the matching section into the worker prompt; read by prompts/implement.md, prompts/verify.md and prompts/worker_agent_common.md (test command / promoted test name).

Rule book (REQ-HON-005..010): residual_vectors[] formatting and delivery rules R-1..R-8 for MITIGATION/WORKAROUND tiers. Consumed by vulnhunter_fix/delivery.py (residual rendering, hand-wave + empty-residual guards), the follow-up-issue renderer, and prompts/worker_agent_crypto.md (R-5 trust-chain residuals) during Phase 3 implement / Phase 5 deliver.

Per-finding worker result (group-NNN_result.json) and the aggregate .vulnfix_result.json (branches[] of results): terminal tier, worker status, bounded tier_judgment, caller routing, discrimination evidence, sweep fields.

Rule book (REQ-GAT-002, REQ-SEC-001, REQ-GAT-008): mask the top-severity word in every delivered text; 5-phrase safe-list. Consumed by scripts/check-severity-mask.py (Gate 1, read-time, pre-deliver) and vulnhunter_fix/delivery.py:SAFE_PHRASE_PATTERNS (write-time, through the worker manual-mask discipline in prompts/worker_agent_common.md).

Rule book (REQ-SWP-001..009): two-pass sibling sweep, per-ROOT summary, routing paths, tier downgrade, column-8 and PR-diff handling. Companion to prompts/sweep.md (Sweep phase, between Verify and Deliver); sweep.md carries invocation, details live here.

Rule book (REQ-SWP-002): CWE-class regex table for Sweep Pass 2 (pattern pass over files Pass 1 did not cover). Consumed by scripts/sweep-root-causes.py and prompts/sweep.md (Sweep phase); also cited by prompts/verify.md.

Rule book (REQ-GRA-016): R1-R5 quality rules for generated security tests and the GOOD/WEAK/WRONG verdict matrix. Enforced by the reviewer-test agent (prompts/reviewer_test.md) during Phase 4 verify (prompts/verify.md); also cited by prompts/worker_agent_common.md when workers write tests in Phase 3.

Per-finding graph sidecar .work/<repo>/graph_context/<vuln>.json written by the executor; workers read it instead of the graph. Closed object; crypto_trust_chain present only for crypto-routed findings.

Rule book (REQ-GRA-011..014): 9-column verification-table shape, cell grammar, column 7/8 semantics, verdict truth table. Read by prompts/verify.md (Phase 4) when building the table; enforced by vulnhunter_fix.delivery.render_verification_table and scripts/validate-verification.py (pre-deliver Gate 6); rendered in templates/pr_body.md and templates/issue_body.md.
Import-time bootstrap: re-executes the calling script under the bundled .venv Python (3.11) when the current interpreter differs, then prepends the venv site-packages and the skill root to sys.path.

Anti-merge grouping check (REQ-GAT-006): allows a multi-finding PR group only when the grouped/split file ratio is at or below the threshold for source or test files. Used in Plan (advisory) and as Gate 5 (--strict).

CLI wrapper around the code graph: builds (or loads cached) graph.json for a repo and, when --findings is given, writes one graph_context/<VULN>.json sidecar per finding (callers of sink, blast radius, confidence).

Gate 2, body completeness (REQ-GAT-003): the PR / issue body must carry every required section heading with non-empty content (headings inside code fences do not count), contain no placeholder tokens, and carry any enforced strings.
Gate 7, committed-test naming (REQ-GAT-013): fails if any file added on the branch is a leaked verify_VULN / exploit_VULN scaffold instead of a repo-convention test name.
Gate 4, idempotency (REQ-GAT-005): every artifact body must carry the vulnfix-key marker; tracking-issue bodies also need the vulnfix-report-id marker.
Gate 3, scope (REQ-GAT-004): every file in the branch's merge-base diff must be in files_modified or be the declared test file. Zero exceptions.
Gate 1, severity mask (REQ-GAT-002): scans artifact bodies for the word stem "critical" (after folding zero-width chars and homoglyphs) outside the safe-phrase list; any hit fails the gate.
Checks whether the authenticated gh user has push access to a GitHub repo (exit 0) or not (exit 1).
Shallow-clones a GitHub repo, or (with --fork) forks it, makes the fork private, enables issues, adds collaborators from collaborators.json and clones the fork.

Canonical cluster scorer for parse_issues Step 3: rejects generic cluster names, scores each cluster by weighted severity counts, sorts by score then member count, and marks the top cluster recommended.

Deterministic completeness-tier classifier (REQ-HON-004): walks WORKAROUND -> MITIGATION -> FULL signals on a diff + fix plan + result and never silently picks FULL; unresolved cases return LLM_REVIEW for tier_judgment.

Mechanical crypto trust-chain checkers (REQ-CWE-009): from the fix diff's added lines, set the four sidecar booleans algorithm_approved, key_source_approved, key_rotation_present, transport_encrypted. Never calls a model.
Mode dispatch for the fix skill: from CWD git origin plus TARGET_REPO / RESULTS_PATH decides in_place, fork, ambiguous or none, and prints one key=value line on stdout.

Dev-time lint (REQ-GAT-003): body templates must carry the headings Gate 2 requires (read from check-body-completeness.py by AST), no template comment may reference a block placeholder, and no Breaking Change heading may carry a suffix that Gate 2's regex rejects.

In-place intake primitives (no gh, no network): extract the three machine markers from an issue body, reconstruct an original body from edit history (unused in v1), enforce one (owner, repo, results_dir) per run, and compute the vulnfix idempotency key.
Detects a target repo's primary language for Plan's worker-prompt adapter routing (REQ-CWE-005): manifest files first, then a file-suffix majority vote.

Parses the tier_judgment model output: first non-comment line is the primary JSON, validated against the tierJudgment $def of references/result-schema.json; an optional TIER_JUDGMENT_SIDECAR comment block is split out.

Regex parser for a VulnHunter results directory: summary-table findings (fallback path; production uses a model extraction), per-finding detail, PoC / exploit-test file discovery, code smells, and vulnfix keys.
Dev-time honesty check for the skill's own PRs: runs the skill's pytest suite with coverage and compares the passed count and coverage percentage claimed in a PR body against the live numbers.

Local-only preflight for the fix skill (no network): tool versions, pinned deps, cloud-LLM env isolation, memory and disk, a fork-mode git-init probe, and in-place clean-tree + worktree prune. Exit 1 on any failed check.
Dev-time lint (REQ-CWE-010): each CWE-class worker prompt must exist and reference worker_agent_common.md, the shared preamble must exist, and the legacy worker_agent.md must be gone.

Gate orchestrator (REQ-GAT-011): loads PR/issue body, result.json and triage sidecar, builds per-gate argv via GATE_ROUTING, runs each mechanical delivery gate as a subprocess, fails closed on missing required gates.
Dev-time lint (REQ-GAT-008): SAFE_PHRASE_PATTERNS in vulnhunter_fix/delivery.py must equal the copy in check-severity-mask.py (compared by AST extraction).
In-place mode: create or reuse a per-finding git worktree at <repo>/.vulnhunter-fix/worktrees/<key>/ on branch vulnfix/<sanitized-slug>, excluding the work dir locally via .git/info/exclude.

Root-cause sweep (REQ-SWP-001..009): for each verified finding, Pass 1 finds graph callers of the sink not routed through the fix, Pass 2 regex-scans the repo with the CWE class's sweep patterns; unmitigated siblings revise the tier to MITIGATION. A missing graph makes the sweep incomplete (exit 3).
Validates a finding (or a parser aggregate with a findings list) against references/finding-schema.json (REQ-SCH-006).
Validates a fix_plan artifact against references/fix_plan-schema.json, with result-schema.json registered for cross-file refs (REQ-SCH-003).
Validates a worker result.json against references/result-schema.json; used at every phase handoff and by the schema-repair loop (REQ-SCH-003/004).
Validates a per-finding triage sidecar (graph_context/<VULN>.json) against references/triage-schema.json before Plan dispatches a worker.

Delivery verification table: header, yes-cell citations and sidecar/result caller coverage. Preserve source edge cases: empty tables can pass; no VULN id skips caller check; citation line 0 is not rejected.
Deterministic Step-5a draft-shape validation: fail at the first violation; extra keys and empty strings are allowed.

PR body must close exactly the expected issue set. Only repeated close keywords are recognized by the actual regex. A bare second number in 'Closes #1, #2' is not recognized, despite the help text claiming both forms count.
